subject: Aurora model — brief on error burst and recovery commitments
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Smith <jared@skylineapp.com>, Skyline Labs Support <support@skylineapp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 Sep 2028 18:12:05 -0700
Subject: Aurora inference — transient spike in 5xx & TIMEOUTs (initial notice)

Hi Jared / Skyline team,

Quick heads-up: we’re seeing a short-lived but high-severity error burst affecting requests routed to the Aurora-6b serving pool in us-west-2. Timeline and facts so far:

- Window: ~18:05–18:30 PDT (ongoing when first observed)
- Symptoms: elevated 5xx rate (503 + upstream TIMEOUT) and increased client-side generation failures
- Peak impact: ~9% error rate against Aurora-6b traffic on the affected nodes; traffic was auto-failed-over to quantized-aurora variants in some routing lanes

Immediate mitigations we’ve applied:
- Circuit breaker triggered on the most impacted cells to limit cascading failures
- Partial routing fallback to quantized variants and to a small warm pool running the previous kernel version
- SRE team is executing a targeted rollback on an optimization kernel suspected to be correlated with the regression

What we need from you:
- Any examples of failed request IDs or timestamps you can share (if available) so we can match them in our logs
- A short note on user-visible impact (number of failed requests/transactions, features affected) to help inform credits and communications

I’m attaching a snapshot from the serving telemetry and a short log sample. We’ll follow up with an ETA for full recovery and a plan for a formal postmortem. Apologies for the disruption — we realize this is customer-impacting and are treating it as high priority.

Attachments: aurora-errburst-20280922.log.gz

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 22 Sep 2028 18:35:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora inference — internal triage notes (kernel rollback in progress)

Olga / Marissa / Karthik — internal ops update, please do not forward raw unless redacted.

What we’ve found so far:
- Correlation: the error spike lines up with a canary rollout of kernel-optimizer v2.3.4 pushed to a subset of the Aurora GPU pool earlier in the afternoon. The kernel introduced a scheduling heuristic that increases eviction pressure for certain sequence-length distributions, which looks to cause TTL/KV cache thrashing and occasional upstream timeouts.
- Current action: rolling back kernel-optimizer to v2.3.3 on affected hosts. The rollback is staged to avoid mass restarts; we’re re-routing a slice of traffic to the warm pool first and then failing over once health checks are stable.
- ETA: we expect baseline behavior to be restored within ~30–45 minutes from now (rollback + health stabilization).

Planned follow-ups:
- Postmortem on Monday; root cause will include a test gap in our canary gating for seq-length skew
- Short term: expand telemetry around cache eviction rates + add an automated rollforward/rollback rule to our canary orchestrator
- Customer remediation: recommend offering a service credit window for the impacted duration; coordinate with finance and sales on the exact amount.

Attachment: rollback-plan-20280922.md

Date: Sat, 23 Sep 2028 09:12:40 -0700
Subject: Aurora incident — recovery confirmed, next steps and postmortem link

Hi Jared / Skyline team — follow-up and recovery summary.

Status: Full recovery confirmed at 08:57 PDT (baseline error rate ~0.2% for Aurora-6b across us-west-2).

Root cause (preliminary):
- A kernel-optimizer change (v2.3.4) introduced a scheduling heuristic that, under a specific sequence-length distribution seen by Skyline traffic, caused disproportionate KV-cache evictions and upstream timeouts.
- The regression slipped past our canary because the canary mix did not include enough long-tail sequence-length examples.

Remediations completed:
- Immediate: rollback to v2.3.3 for the affected pool and gradual traffic re-introduction; circuit breaker rules relaxed after health checks passed.
- Short-term engineering fixes: improved canary coverage, additional eviction-rate alerts, and a throttling tweak to reduce cache churn under skewed distributions.
- Permanent fix: a patch to the scheduler logic is scheduled for 2028-10-01 alongside an expanded staged rollout plan and stricter automated rollback thresholds.

Customer commitments:
- We’re preparing a formal postmortem and will share the link once finalized (draft accessible here: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/postmortems/aurora-2028-09-22).
- We will credit Skyline Labs for the impacted usage window (18:05–18:57 PDT on 2028-09-22). Finance will follow up with the exact credit amount and timing — I’ve opened INC-4821 to track billing remediation.

Immediate asks for Skyline:
- Confirmation that you’ve observed restored behavior on your side (if you can verify a couple of previously failing request IDs)
- Any additional business impact notes you’d like included in the postmortem (customer escalations, SLA effects)

Again — sorry for the disruption. We take reliability very seriously and will incorporate learnings to reduce the chance of recurrence. I’ll be your point of contact for postmortem and credits.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.ai
